text:
sarah.dev: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a routing-config linter + JSON/YAML schema for the API gateway. Want early feedback before I wire it into the Console editor and CI.

matt.platform: Love it. Are you leaning JSON Schema (AJV) or a custom validator?

sarah.dev: AJV + JSON Schema for core shape, and a tiny policy layer for precedence rules. Plan: accept YAML or JSON in the editor, convert to JSON, run AJV, then run the policy checks (headers, overrides, precedence).

anya-console: For the Console UX, can we do "preview validation" that doesn't block save by default? non-blocking warnings are nicer for power users. Also need a "strict mode" toggle for orgs that want enforceable configs. :gear:

matt.platform: Agreed on strict toggle. For CI/lint we should fail builds by default if strict enabled. Suggest we publish the schema as an npm package (redwood-routing-schema) so libs/clients and CI share the same source of truth.

dino-ml: One gotcha: header-based routing + overrides create combinatorial cases. We should model precedence explicitly: 1) exact path+header match, 2) path prefix+header, 3) path-only, 4) default. Schema should validate that routes define an explicit fallback or mark "fallback: true" for exactly one route.

sarah.dev: Good point. I added a policy rule that requires exactly one fallback route. Here's a minimal example I put in the PR branch (YAML):

```yaml
routes:
  - id: users-v1
    match:
      path: "/v1/users"
      headers:
        X-Canary: "true"
    destination: users-service:v1
  - id: users-default
    match:
      path_prefix: "/v1/users"
    destination: users-service:v1
    fallback: true
```

matt.platform: Nice and readable. In the schema we should validate that `match.path` is either a plain string or a valid regex string when prefixed with `re:`. e.g. `re:^/v[0-9]+/users$`. Use AJV's custom format for regex.

anya-console: For the editor I'd like to show inline hints: which fields are required (destination, match.*), warnings for overlapping route definitions (same path+headers), and a small "test request" UI to evaluate which route would be picked for a sample request. That helps ops sanity-check before saving.

sarah.dev: I mocked up a test harness that runs the exact routing algorithm locally and prints the selected route. It's used by the lint step too. CLI usage: `rw-routing-lint validate ./my-route.yaml --sample "GET /v1/users X-Canary:true"`.

matt.platform: Can you add unit tests that cover header precedence, wildcard host matching, and header normalization (case-insensitive)? Those are frequent failures in other gateways.

sarah.dev: Yup — writing table-driven tests now. Also adding a small property-based test for random header sets to catch edge cases.

dino-ml: One more: quotas and per-route quotas need to be a separate section in the schema, not inline in the route def, to avoid accidental per-tenant leakage. Could be `quotas: [ {route_id, qps, burst} ]` with a cross-reference validation step.

matt.platform: Cross-ref validation can be a second pass after AJV (AJV can't do inter-array reference checks easily). Implement as `validateCrossRefs(schemaJson)` in the linter.

sarah.dev: That fits the plan. I'll split validation into stages: 1) AJV (shape + field formats), 2) cross-ref & policy checks, 3) deterministic routing sim. Console will surface results from all stages.

deploy-bot: CI: routing-schema lint job failed on branch `feat/routing-lint` — 1 error. Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/build/1145 (private)

matt.platform: @sarah.dev can you check CI? probably a schema edge-case in the example fixtures.

sarah.dev: Found it — one fixture had `fallback: true` on two routes. Fixing and pushing a tiny patch.

deploy-bot: CI: rerun successful — routing-schema lint job passed on commit `a1b2c3d`. :white_check_mark:

anya-console: Awesome. Next steps for Console: 1) embed lint results under the Save button, 2) show quick-fix suggestions (e.g., "mark single fallback route"), 3) allow toggling strict mode per-organization. I'll draft a mock.

matt.platform: Ops: remember to document migration path for existing configs. We should provide `rw-routing-lint migrate` that emits normalized configs and a changelog of breaking changes.

sarah.dev: Adding migrate cmd to the CLI. Also I'll open an RFC describing schema decisions (regex format, header match semantics, fallback rule). Link will go in the PR.

dino-ml: If you want me to run some heavy combinatorial tests (hundreds of thousands of random routes) I can spin up a job to check routing determinism across changes.

sarah.dev: That would be hugely helpful — thanks. I pushed the schema to `github.com/redwood/routing-schemas` on `feat/routing-lint` with unit tests and examples. Please review the PR and the console mock from @anya-console.

matt.platform: Reviewing now. Let's try to get this merged before the next Dedicated rollout so that customers can use the strict mode.

sarah.dev: Thanks everyone — will post PR link and add to eng-review calendar. :rocket:
